citation: Spanhol FA, Oliveira LS, Petitjean C, Heutte L. A Dataset for Breast Cancer Histopathological Image Classification. IEEE TBME.
evidence_role: Defines dataset decision task and class semantics
key_extracted_evidence: BreaKHis is a histopathological benign-vs-malignant tumor image dataset; this anchors the matrix to tissue-level cancer-support classification, not screening mammography alone.
uncertainty_or_limits: Dataset paper does not provide clinical cost ratios.

citation: Breast Cancer Histopathological Database (BreaKHis), UFPR VRI.
evidence_role: Clinical semantics of benign and malignant labels
key_extracted_evidence: Official documentation states malignant tumor is cancer and can invade, metastasize, and cause death; benign tumors do not match malignancy criteria and are relatively localized/slow-growing.
uncertainty_or_limits: Dataset documentation, not an outcomes registry or cost-utility source.

citation: National Cancer Institute. Breast Cancer Screening (PDQ), Health Professional Version.
population_or_context: Screening and diagnostic consequences; used as secondary proxy
evidence_role: Quantifies false-positive workup burden and missed/interval cancer harm
key_extracted_evidence: NCI summarizes harms including false positives, biopsies, overdiagnosis, and false negatives; interval cancers tend to have worse prognosis and may be higher grade or receptor negative.
uncertainty_or_limits: Screening evidence is a secondary proxy for histopathology decision support; not a direct BreaKHis cost matrix.

citation: Nelson HD, et al. Harms of Breast Cancer Screening: Systematic Review to Update the 2009 USPSTF Recommendation.
evidence_role: Bounds low-cost false-positive harm as real but typically less severe than missed malignancy
key_extracted_evidence: USPSTF harms review is used for false-positive downstream burden such as additional imaging, biopsy, and anxiety; this prevents treating benign-as-malignant errors as costless.
uncertainty_or_limits: Screening false positives differ from histopathology decision-support false positives.

citation: National Cancer Institute. Breast Cancers Between Mammograms Have Aggressive Features.
population_or_context: Interval breast cancers as proxy for missed/delayed detection
evidence_role: Supports high time-sensitivity and irreversibility for malignant-as-benign errors
key_extracted_evidence: NCI reports interval breast cancers are more likely to show aggressive features, including higher stage and grade, larger size, and receptor-negative status.

citation: Elmore JG, et al. Diagnostic concordance among pathologists interpreting breast biopsy specimens. JAMA.
key_extracted_evidence: Breast biopsy interpretation has measurable diagnostic variability, especially outside straightforward invasive cancer/benign extremes; supports using sensitivity analysis rather than asserting a unique exact cost ratio.
uncertainty_or_limits: Concordance study informs diagnostic uncertainty, not direct patient-harm costs.

citation: Dillon MF, et al. The Accuracy of Ultrasound, Stereotactic, and Clinical Core Biopsies in the Diagnosis of Breast Cancer, With an Analysis of False-Negative Cases.
key_extracted_evidence: False-negative biopsy results can delay cancer diagnosis; multidisciplinary review/triple assessment reduces delay, supporting the decision-support caveat that human review can mitigate but not erase false-negative harm.
uncertainty_or_limits: Core biopsy process differs from image-classifier decision support and BreaKHis excisional biopsy images.

citation: False-negative core needle biopsies of the breast: analysis of clinical, radiologic, and pathologic findings in missed cancer cases.
population_or_context: False-negative breast core needle biopsy cases
evidence_role: Supports delay/irreversibility score for malignant-as-benign errors
key_extracted_evidence: Reports missed breast cancers and diagnosis delays in a false-negative biopsy context, supporting high cost for malignant tissue called benign.
uncertainty_or_limits: Older and procedure-specific; used as secondary pathology-adjacent evidence.
